items.title: The Chicago PMI unexpectedly collapsed to 47.1 in August from 57.6 in July. Analysts had expected a rise to 59. This is the lowest reading since December 2025, but more significantly the biggest downside surprise since February 2015. The economy is far weaker than most believe.

items.title: The U.S. goods trade deficit swelled 18% in July to $118.8 billion, the largest since tariff front-running in March 2025, as imports jumped 3.7% and exports fell 2.9%. Excluding tariff-distorted months, it's the biggest since COVID reopening demand boosted imports in March 2022.

items.title: Rising bond yields are the market's way of telling the U.S. government it has a debt problem that needs to be solved before a crisis hits. Just as pain lets you know there is a medical problem that needs attention, if you simply numb the pain so you don't have to feel it, the underlying condition gets worse. If it gets bad enough, it can be fatal. Numbing the pain is precisely what the Trump administration is trying to do now with Operation Twist. As a result, the eventual sovereign debt crisis may be fatal for the dollar and the U.S. economy.

items.title: In Warsh’s first two months as Fed chair, M2 has grown about 0.9%, an annualized pace of nearly 6%. Properly defined, inflation is the expansion of the money supply; higher prices are the consequence. A 6% monetary inflation rate is hardly consistent with the Fed's 2% CPI target.
